name: The tag on the instrument
oneLine: A hairline vernier caliper drawn flat across the page, its jaws closed on one real figure from the table, with a shop-floor calibration tag wired to it that prints what was tested, where, and — in a hatched block with real area — what was not.
threeSecondRead: That is a measuring tool with a paper tag tied to it — this page is treating a person the way a lab treats an instrument.
The tag names what was tested and where; the shaded block near the bottom is the part that was deliberately not tested.
There is no percentage and no fill anywhere — the number was read off a scale against a limit, not set by whoever drew it.
form:
A `<figure>` in `#skills > .inner`, between `<header>` and `<Bench />`. It absorbs the lede: `skillsContent.lede` is deleted from the header and replaced by a `<figcaption>` above the drawing in `--font-heading`, `clamp(1.05rem,1.6vw,1.35rem)`, `--white` — "Nothing here is self-rated." (first two words carry it; NN/g layer-cake). Grid: `minmax(0,480px) 1fr`, `gap: clamp(1.5rem,4vw,3rem)`, `align-items:center`, `contain: layout paint`.

LEFT — the instrument, inline SVG `viewBox="0 0 480 200"`, `aspect-ratio:480/200`, `shape-rendering:crispEdges`, ticks at `n+0.5`. Built from `line/rect/polyline/polygon/text/circle` only — **no `<path>`**, so `tests/e2e/skills.spec.ts:139` (`#skills svg path` count 20) survives untouched. Four-weight ramp, nothing between: `--ink-500` 0.5 (micro ticks), `--mist-400` 0.75 (minor ticks, leader, vernier), `--mist-200` 1.25 (beam, jaws, spec bracket), `--white` 1.5 (the reading). Beam: y=96, x 60→460, with a `--ink-900` 0.5px line at y=97 beneath it so the scale sits *in* the surface, not on it (device #15) — used here only. Scale = milliseconds, 1 ms = 1 px, 0 at x=60. Three tick tiers rising from the beam: major every 100 ms, h=14, numbered `0 100 200 300 400` in `--font-mono` 10px `--mist-400`, `letter-spacing .06em`; minor every 25 ms, h=8; micro every 5 ms **only between 150–250 ms**, h=4 — you engrave finer where you read. Above 200 ms, an outer bracket in `--mist-200` 1.25 with butt-capped 6px serifs, labelled `TL 200 ms` (ILAC-G8 tolerance-limit vocabulary). Sliding vernier: `<rect>` 66×34 at y=100, fill `var(--card-bg)`, stroke `--mist-400` 1px, `rx=0`; 11 ticks at 4.5 px pitch against the 5 ms micro pitch → **least count 0.5 ms**, printed as `LC 0.5 ms` in mono 9px. Fixed jaw drops 22px from x=60; the moving jaw drops from the slider's left edge; between them the measured span. Exactly one vernier tick coincides with one main tick — that pair, plus a 1px vertical joining them from y=82 to y=112, is the only `--gold` in the drawing. The specimen is real: `capabilities[2]`, "Real-time telemetry platforms · 10,000+ concurrent devices held at P95 under 200 ms · ANZ". The jaws close on the *limit*, 200 ms, because skills.ts claims "under 200 ms" and never states a P95 value — inventing one would be a fabricated fact.

RIGHT — the tag, HTML not SVG (Bench's own HTML-rails/SVG-wires idiom), so type stays selectable and the real `<Caliper>` component supplies gold. A `<dl>`, square corners, `1px solid var(--card-border)`, six 0.5px `--card-border` rules, a 3px punched eyelet on its left edge that the SVG's leader line (two segments, 30° then a 5 mm horizontal landing, `--mist-400` 0.75) lands on. Labels mono uppercase 10px `--mist-400` `letter-spacing .10em`; values 11px `--mist-200`; figures `--font-heading`. Fields: `CALIBRATION CERTIFICATE` / `1 OF 17` (`capabilities.length`) · `ITEM` · `METHOD` · `RESULT` = `<Caliper state="sourced">200 ms</Caliper>` · `TAKEN AT` ANZ Banking Group + kind badge `PROGRAMME` (from `sources`) · `NOT TESTED` = `<Caliper state="open">` over the 45° hatch, printing `capabilities[16]`'s "AWS and GCP — studying; no certificate issued", given a full field's area · `CERT No. 16b856c0 · 157,615 BYTES` from `cvFingerprint` · `DUE` — an empty ruled box, because ISO/IEC 17025 §7.8.4.3 forbids a lab asserting a recalibration date the customer never requested.
motion:
Trigger: the exact IntersectionObserver block from `Bench.tsx:189-207` — `threshold: 0.15`, `observer.disconnect()` on first hit, and a `matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)')` early return that sets `drawn = true`. Three beats, 1,940 ms trigger→settled, inside the 2.4 s budget.

Beat 1 (0–640 ms) — the slider travels 96 px and **stops**: `transform: translateX()` on the slider `<g>` (compositor-only, `transform-box: fill-box`), `640ms` on a **new token `--motion-ease-mechanical: cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1)`** declared in `globals.css`. This is non-negotiable: `--motion-ease-emphasized` overshoots, and a caliper jaw that bounces is a broken caliper. `--motion-` is on the audit's approved non-colour prefix list, so the token passes gate 9.

Beat 2 (560–1,180 ms, 80 ms overlap) — the coincidence resolves. The two coinciding ticks cross-fade `--mist-400 → --gold` over 240 ms `var(--motion-ease-standard)`; the vertical reading line traces `stroke-dashoffset: 1 → 0` with `pathLength="1"`, `380ms var(--motion-ease-emphasized)` — the emphasized curve is correct *here* because this is ink arriving, not a mechanism moving.

Beat 3 (1,180–1,860 ms) — the tag rules itself in. Six 1px-tall rules wipe `clip-path: inset(0 100% 0 0) → inset(0)`, `260ms var(--motion-ease-emphasized)`, staggered `calc(var(--i) * 34ms)` with `--i` set inline (`style={{ '--i': i }}`, the Bench idiom, invisible to the token audit). Only the rules animate — no text moves, so zero reflow and zero CLS, and each clipped box is 1px tall so the paint cost of `clip-path` is nil. The `NOT TESTED` hatch and the empty `DUE` box are the last two to land: measured evidence first, admitted gap second (Aronson's pratfall ordering — the flaw only pays out after competence is established).

Settle at 1,940 ms: `setSettled(true)` flips `animation: none` on everything, and every resting style already equals its final frame. The effect is gated on `[drawn]` with no measurement dependency, so a resize or orientation change can never replay the explainer under the reader.
states:
**Reduced motion:** motion is authored as the enhancement, not an override — base styles *are* the settled frame, and the entire intro lives inside `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)`, so a missed selector fails static rather than animated. The JS branch additionally sets `drawn = true` at mount so nothing waits on the observer. All three beats survive as layout: slider parked at its reading, coincidence already gold, tag fully ruled, hatch and empty DUE box present. No `<canvas>` anywhere, so `TC-CINE-04` (canvas count 0 under `reduce`) passes by construction.

**390px:** below 900px — the same breakpoint Bench already uses — the grid collapses to one column and a single `matchMedia` boolean swaps the SVG's `viewBox` to `"120 40 220 160"`, cropping to the fine 150–250 ms window: the jaws, the vernier, the coincidence and the reading, all at roughly double effective size. The leader line swaps to a vertical two-segment variant off the same boolean. The tag goes full width with labels stacked above values. No geometry is measured, so there is nothing to re-measure and nothing to shift.

**Keyboard / screen reader:** nothing focusable is added, so no new focus-ring or tab-order surface. The SVG is `aria-hidden="true" focusable="false"` (Bench's choice) because every fact it draws is also real text in the tag beside it. The tag is a `<dl>` inside `<figure role="group">` with the `<figcaption>` as its name. `RESULT` carries the real `<Caliper state="sourced">`, whose visually-hidden gloss speaks "Measured; source given."; `NOT TESTED` carries `<Caliper state="open">`, speaking "Not measurable; reason given." The empty `DUE` box is a drawn `<span aria-hidden="true">` plus visually-hidden text: "Left blank — a laboratory may not state a recalibration date the customer has not requested." No `role="status"` and no live region, so `TC-SKILL-07` (`#skills [role="status"]` count 1) is unaffected.

**No JS:** the tag is server-rendered markup and is complete on its own; the SVG renders its full settled geometry from static coordinates — there is no measurement pass, unlike Bench, so the un-hydrated first paint *is* the final paint. The only thing JS adds is the intro and the sub-900px viewBox swap; without it the desktop framing shows on narrow screens, which is degraded but truthful.
coherence:
It extends the site's three existing devices and adds no fourth. The `<Caliper>` component is used unmodified in two of its three states — `sourced` on the RESULT field, `open` on NOT TESTED — so gold arrives through the one component that already gets gold right, and the reader spends no new learning budget (R9). The 45° hatch is the same mark the open caliper and Compass's role-derived sectors already use, so a reader who has met it twice already knows what the NOT TESTED block means. It reuses Bench's IntersectionObserver `drawn`/`settled` two-flag shape, its inline `--i` stagger idiom, its `pathLength={1}` normalisation, and its HTML-object/SVG-annotation split.

Deliberately avoided: **About/Compass** owns every circle, bezel, dial, rotating ring and "index fixed at twelve o'clock" — this is strictly linear, contains one 3px eyelet punch and nothing else round, and inverts Compass's grammar (there the ring turns and the index is fixed; here the scale is fixed and the reading position travels). **Experience** owns horizontal proportional bars on a 16-year axis — this is a graduated millisecond rule with three tick tiers, no fill, and nothing whose length encodes a magnitude of his. **Vitrine** owns hairline mechanism drawings including a drawn caliper, so: no boxes, no arrows between boxes, no `currentColor` (this uses an explicit four-weight token ramp), and the tag is set type rather than a drawn illustration. **Bench** owns wires and rails — there is exactly one leader line here, it has a drafting landing segment, and it is grey, never gold.

Gold appears in exactly two places, both terminators, never paths: the single coinciding vernier pair with its reading line, and the closed jaws of the `sourced` Caliper on the RESULT field. Both are literally "this figure has a source you can go and check" — the vernier's whole mechanism *is* the gold rule, since precision arrives from a claim coinciding with an independent reference. No gold on the tag border, the hatch, the leader, the numerals, or on hover. `MONO-05` (gold must render in `#skills`) stays satisfied; every colour is a `var()`, so no raw hex enters the static audit.
risks: Near-miss with Vitrine: `Drawings.tsx:284-293` already draws a caliper closing on a reading. Mine is larger, carries scales and a tag, and is stylistically separated (token ramp vs `currentColor`, type vs illustration) — but if a reviewer reads them as the same device, this concept is spending a coin another section already spent.

The vernier coincidence is the whole idea and it is a two-pixel event. Below roughly 340px of effective drawing width it stops being visible, which is why the mobile path crops rather than scales; if the crop is ever dropped, the metaphor silently dies on phones while still looking fine.

A reader may read `200 ms` as a score. The mitigation is the `TL 200 ms` bracket and the `LC 0.5 ms` label making it unmistakably an instrument reading against a limit — but if the caption or the bracket is edited away later, the figure reverts to looking like a rating.

It adds roughly 260px of height to a section whose own source comment says motion here is "deliberately nil" and the screen should be "flat, dense and silent." Deleting the three-line lede pays for most of that, and the intro is one small gesture that settles dead — but this is a real tension with a written intent, not an imagined one.

The specimen is one row out of seventeen. If a reader concludes only that row is evidenced, the figure has backfired; the `1 OF 17` field and the Bench directly beneath are what stop that, and both must stay.

`clip-path` is a paint-property animation. It is safe only because each animated box is 1px tall and it runs once, then stops. If someone later moves the wipe onto the tag's text or its full-height panel, it becomes a real scroll-time cost.
whyBest:
It is the only option that makes the section title stop being a puzzle. A visitor who has never heard "calibration" still recognises a measuring tool with a paper tag wired to it — that recognition happens at image speed, before any reading, and it converts "Calibration card" from an unfamiliar term into a label for something already understood. Every text-first alternative asks the reader to learn the word first and the object second, which is the exact split-attention failure the section currently has: the metaphor is explained in a lede that sits above and apart from the thing it names.

It answers all three questions with one object instead of three devices. What a calibration card *is*: a tag that ships attached to an instrument. What it means *here*: the tag's fields are the table's columns, so the drawing is a legend for the grid below it without being a detached legend — the #1 measured killer, avoided. Why not skill bars: an instrument that reads by coincidence with an independent reference visibly has two scales, and a proficiency bar has one and nothing to check it against. That refutation is a physical fact about the drawing, not an argument printed next to it.

It is the cheapest concept to make true. Every value on the tag is a field that already exists in `skills.ts` and `cv-fingerprint.ts`; nothing is derived, interpolated or invented, and the one place where a number could have been fabricated — a P95 figure — is resolved by closing the jaws on the *limit* the data actually claims, which is metrology's own "at the points tested" hedge rather than a compromise.

And it puts the honest gap where it earns the most. `NOT TESTED · AWS · GCP` gets a full ruled field with real hatched area, arriving last, after the sourced reading — the ordering the pratfall and blemishing results demand, and the inverse of burying it at the bottom of a table. Beside it sits an empty `DUE` box that the document refuses to fill in. That empty box is the entire thesis of the section in one rectangle: an instrument's authority comes from stating its own boundary, and a boundary is a shape you can draw.
